# pysacd-extract: a drop-in replacement for sacd_extract

`pysacd-extract` takes `sacd_extract`'s options and writes the same files,
with the same names and the same bytes.

## Migrating

```sh
ln -s "$(command -v pysacd-extract)" ~/bin/sacd_extract    # that's the whole migration
```

Scripts, `sacd_extract.cfg` (including `logging=1`) and muscle memory keep
working:

```console
$ pysacd-extract -2 -m -s -i album.iso       # DSF, stereo + multichannel
$ pysacd-extract -e -C -i album.iso          # DSDIFF edit master + cue + xml
$ pysacd-extract -P -i album.iso             # disc information, as sacd_extract prints it
$ pysacd-extract -I -s -i 192.0.2.10:2002    # copy a PS3 disc and extract it, one pass over the network
```

Front ends that run `sacd_extract`, such as
[sacd-extract-gui](https://github.com/amstelchen/sacd-extract-gui) and
SACDExtractGUI (its original repository is gone), work unchanged:
point their executable setting at `pysacd-extract`. Programs written in Python
don't need a separate process at all; see [the Python library](library.md).

## Compatibility policy

Differences from `sacd_extract` are treated as bugs. The exceptions below are
deliberate:

| Where | sacd_extract | pysacd-extract | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Two discs aimed at one folder (sets mastered as 1/1, e.g. *Live-Evil*) | mixes them silently, and overwrites tracks whose names match | writes the second disc to `<album> [<catalogue no.>]` and warns; `--disc N/M` gives sacd_extract's own `Disc N` layout | silent mixing is a bug (#4) |
| Hostile disc text (invisible characters such as controls, bidi and zero-width characters, tag characters or U+2028; `` ` $ ; ``; a leading `-`) | copied into names, tags, cue, XML and `-P` as is | neutralised: invisible characters removed (a control becomes a space) and shown as escapes in `-P`; ordinary discs are unaffected | [security](security.md#hostile-text) |
| Malformed TOC timing (a track running past its area's playtime, a zero-length track, more audio than the area's sectors can hold) | uses the times as given: writes a header-only file for a zero-length track and only the frames it finds | cuts tracks to the playtime (so `-P` and the files show the cut times), stops with an error on a zero-length track or on more audio than the image's sectors can hold | no real disc does this; a hostile one could ask for hours of output ([security](security.md#hostile-images)) |
| Korean (KSC 5601) and Chinese GB 2312 disc text | written into names, tags and cue sheets as the raw disc bytes, which aren't UTF-8 | decoded, and written as UTF-8 | names that aren't UTF-8 break most tools and can't be written on macOS or Windows. Shift-JIS and Big5 discs, which `sacd_extract` decodes, are byte-identical (`tests/test_names.py`, #47) |
| Raw-sector images (2064/2054 bytes per sector) | refused | read; `-I` writes a plain ISO | real rips exist in that form |
| A dropped PS3 connection | gives up | reconnects and resumes, after checking it's still the same disc | PS3 drives are flaky |
| Running as root | runs | runs, with a one-line warning | `sacd_extract` users run it with `sudo`; [security](security.md#running-as-root) |
| An image cut short inside the audio | stops at the cut, writing what it has | reads up to the cut and writes the rest of each track as silence (counted as missing frames, exit status 1) | scarletbook's reading of the specification: positions it can't find are missing frames |
| A DST frame the specification calls invalid (for example a code value out of range, sacd-spec corpus `dst-code-all-ones`) | decodes it anyway, into undefined audio | fills it with 0x55, as for any undecodable frame, warns, and counts it as a DST error (exit status 1) | the frame has no defined audio; since 0.3.0 scarletbook decodes, and it applies the specification's validity rules |
| `-b` (pauses) | cuts on sectors, so a boundary frame can land in both tracks | cuts on frame timecodes | gapless and unambiguous |
| DSDIFF "creating machine" comment; `.cue`/`.xml` version lines | name sacd-ripper | name pysacd | honesty; otherwise byte-identical |
| Console messages | | `-P` and the cfg summary are identical; other lines are worded differently | |

## Extensions

Extensions are long options only, so they never collide with `sacd_extract`'s
short ones:

- `--flac`, `--wav`: PCM output, gapless, 24-bit;
- `--musicbrainz`: tags and cover art;
- `--submit-isrcs` (with `--musicbrainz`): offer the disc's ISRCs to the
  matched release, asking first ([details](converting.md#submitting-isrcs-to-musicbrainz));
- `--templates`: your own folder and file naming;
- `--threads`;
- `--exact`: for a track far into an area, read the area up to it instead of starting
  provisionally ([why](development.md#the-audio-through-scarletbook));
- `--disc N/M`: place a disc mastered as 1/1 into a set;
- `--log-file`, `--log-level`: see [logging](logging.md).

Run `pysacd-extract --help` for the full list.

## Don't take our word for it

```sh
mkdir a b
(cd a && sacd_extract   -2 -m -s -i ../album.iso)
(cd b && pysacd-extract -2 -m -s -i ../album.iso)
diff -r a b && echo identical
```

The same comparison runs in CI on every pull request. On a library of real
discs:

- **`-P` disc information:** identical on **99 of 99** plain-SACD images.
- **Output trees:** **28 of 28** end-to-end cases byte-identical. They cover
  every cfg mode, `-o`/`-y`, `-z`, `-k`, `-b`, `-I -w`, 5-channel areas,
  multi-disc sets, titles with trailing spaces, a disc with no text, DSDIFF
  edit masters, cue and XML.
- **DST:** **6,676,925 frames** (27 areas, about 24.7 hours) decoded with no
  errors.
- **Full DST syntax:** every optional feature, forced by a test-only encoder
  at 2, 5 and 6 channels, gives identical results from the original, pysacd
  and `sacd_extract`.
- **PCM:** matches FFmpeg's DSD decoder to −104 dB below 20 kHz. Tracks join
  sample-exactly.

Speed comparisons are in [performance](performance.md).
